prompts.task: Exercise only the exact shipped Python CLI launcher policy using ./service/eval/inputs/python-cli-launcher-policy-cases.json and the loaded otel-instrument Python language guide. This is a bounded executable wrapper-interface check, not instrumentation of the Flask app. Read the actual fixture/source receipts, then copy the first bash fence after ## Auto-Instrumentation (CLI Wrapper) from the loaded guide byte-for-byte into ./service/.observe/cli-launcher/otel-entrypoint.sh. Record guide path/hash, heading/fence selection and extracted-shell hash; do not replace its policy with a corrected implementation. Use only stdlib/POSIX tooling already available. Create a temporary fake opentelemetry-instrument and harmless fake app under .observe, following the input fake_instrumentor_contract: the CLI only records effective argv/environment, consumes and records every documented value-taking flag including --logs_exporter when present, distinguishes CLI overrides from raw child environment, invokes the remaining original fake-app command once and returns its exit code. The fake app records its exact received argument vector, emits both original sink markers and exits with the case app_exit_code. Neither fake may enforce or repair wrapper log policy. Run every supplied case in a fresh allowlisted environment with a bounded timeout; store actual subprocess command/returncode/stdout/stderr and instrumentor/app invocation/config receipts. Do not merely describe expected cases, grep patterns or mark a future probe as completed. Preserve argument boundaries including spaces, literal dollar text and an empty argument. Check normal local HTTP endpoint/path/port derivation and independent signal endpoint/protocol precedence including gRPC; exercise each header source independently and together, non-local destinations and unsupported logs protocol. Determine from actual effective child configuration whether a fault skips only the newly added local log path while preserving application execution, trace/metric settings, original sinks and operator header/endpoint values. Identify a child-only none/bridge-disable safety guard as conflict isolation, not user opt-out; never persist it as the normal profile. Separately exercise actual explicit none and another exporter as operator-owned branches. Materialize only the supplied normal profile under .observe and prove it and parent environment stay unchanged across the fault cases. Capture only the provided synthetic auth sentinels, and assert those values are absent from actual stdout/stderr. Save an addressable machine-readable ./service/.observe/python-cli-launcher-policy.json containing all observed cases and assertions plus concise Markdown if useful. Unsupported/missing interface execution or actual failing cases must be reported honestly, not patched around; this task cannot establish installed OTel support, exporter construction, native telemetry, Studio/cloud receipt or latest registry facts. A later actual dependency application would still require task-time newest-compatible runtime/constraint/API inspection and exact checked specs/lock, not any fixed library release threshold or this fake CLI. Do not execute/import/modify app.py, real dependencies, manifests/lockfiles, inputs, skills, tests or global configuration; do not install packages, run the real Flask app/model/collector, contact registry/cloud/network, use browser/computer-use/UI or open saved reports. Only .observe fixture-side harness/output artifacts and their harmless local child executions are authorized.

judge_inputs: Read the loaded Python language guide at the actor source hash, supplied synthetic case input and actual generated harness, extracted shell, raw per-case process/instrumentor/app receipts, normal.env, python-cli-launcher-policy.json, last_message.md and grade.json. Inspect exact source behavior rather than accepting assertions or pattern matches. Original fixture app/manifest/Makefile and inputs must remain unchanged.

Return exactly one ordered check per six criteria with IDs rubric-1 through rubric-6; do not merge or omit independent obligations. Equivalent precise MD/JSON layout is valid, but the required machine-readable observed case ledger and actual executions must exist. Judge completed receipts; do not execute a new app, probe, installation or network check.

The fake instrumentor/app are execution instruments only: they must not implement header/endpoint/protocol guards, edit effective environment, fake received telemetry or force expected results. CLI argv/environment evidence proves wrapper policy forwarding and process isolation only; never demand or accept actual SDK exporter/LogRecord/receiver/cloud claims from it. Child-only conflict guards are permitted to set logs exporter none and disable the zero-code bridge while preserving original operator values; that is not permission to write none into the normal profile or parent environment. Effective exporter selection must account for documented CLI flag precedence: --logs_exporter none can safely disable the CLI log branch while preserving OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp in the original child environment. Do not fail this equivalent forwarding merely because the environment variable remains otlp, or accept false success based on environment alone when a CLI override differs. Fake app environment is a recorded observation, not a substitute for parsed CLI interface values.
rubric: Uses the exact current shipped CLI-wrapper shell from the loaded Python guide fence, with reproducible source/extracted hashes and no semantic guard changes. Creates a fake instrumentor that only records documented CLI flags/effective synthetic environment and launches the harmless fake app, plus real bounded subprocess executions of every supplied case with addressable raw command/exit/stdout/stderr and instrumentor/app receipts. Preserves original fixture/input/skill/global files and performs no real app/dependency/network/SDK or UI work. A reimplemented guard, fabricated observations, static pattern assertion or plan-only matrix fails this criterion.

Actual normal executions enable local OTLP logs when exporter is absent or otlp, keep the zero-code bridge eligible, accept empty header variables, and derive exactly http://127.0.0.1:55328/collector/v1/logs from the configured generic trace endpoint without losing its nondefault port/base path or duplicating signal paths. The explicit local log endpoint http://127.0.0.1:55329/v1/logs wins and retains its protocol. Normal gRPC inherits http://127.0.0.1:55327 without /v1/logs, while a separate log HTTP protocol/endpoint remains independent from generic gRPC. No hardcoded fallback replaces configured local routes or corrupts generic/trace/metric configuration.

Actual independently executed generic-header, logs-header and both-header cases each block only the added local log exporter/zero-code bridge, including the both-header case with an explicit local signal endpoint. The fake app/instrumentor still run once, original sink markers appear, and the app exit code is returned rather than a wrapper abort. Effective child trace/metric exporters/endpoints/headers, generic and signal-specific operator header values remain preserved; no auth sentinel appears in actual stdout/stderr. The wrapper emits a value-free conflict diagnostic instead of enabling merged credential inheritance or silently treating the fault as normal success.

Actual non-local generic destination, non-local logs endpoint and unsupported logs-protocol cases each report the local-log boundary conflict and skip only that added log path before the instrumentor/app continue. Their endpoint/protocol/header values and existing trace/metric settings remain operator-owned and intact; no cloud log route is enabled, no unsupported logs protocol is forwarded as an active added local pipeline, and no conflict aborts or replaces app execution. A child-only --logs_exporter none option or environment none guard, together with bridge-disable, is an acceptable CLI isolation mechanism when evidenced and not persisted. Do not fail unrelated trace/metric routes to suppress logs.

Actual explicit none disables the added zero-code log bridge without validating or rewriting its operator-owned endpoint/protocol/headers; actual explicit console exporter preserves its exporter and operator-owned OTEL_PYTHON_LOG_AUTO_INSTRUMENTATION value, with no added local route/bridge or endpoint-policy validation. Both preserve original command argument vectors including spaces/literal dollar/empty arguments, app exit7 and original stdout/stderr sink markers. Every case invokes exactly the supplied fake app once with unchanged original arguments and preserves its selected exit code; wrapper-added instrumentor options are distinguished from app arguments.

Keeps the normal generated .observe/cli-launcher/normal.env at OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp with the supplied local signal endpoint/protocol before and after every fault/opt-out probe, and proves parent environment unchanged. Clearly separates explicit user opt-out from child-only conflict isolation and records incomplete local logs honestly. Final artifacts distinguish executed exact-shell/fake-interface evidence from unexecuted installed SDK/API, native telemetry, receiver/cloud and current-registry proof. Any later real dependency application requires task-time newest-compatible selection under actual runtime/manifest/operator/lock constraints, current public API/capability inspection, immutable checked apply and resulting installed comparison; fixed library thresholds and fake CLI behavior cannot substitute. No default none, fabricated receiver proof or real credential exposure closes a case.
